verdict: The hub reads as a cluttered prototype: the station labels are huge and compete with each other, the HUD text is tiny, the accents don't follow the style guide, and the hotbar is heavy for a hub.

findings.where: station labels (wirt the gambler, enter raid!, the mainframe, shop craft and hire, settings, the stash, the last pour, fashion)
findings.what: Every label is about 36px in dark boxes at the same weight, so the eye hits eight equal blocks and 'enter raid!' (the one primary action) does not stand out. The labels are also about twice the 20px body size in the guide, and they cover the NPCs and stations they name. The '!' is a loud tone and the labels have no hierarchy.
findings.fix: Drop the labels to 20px f-cond 600 on a --ui-panel pill with 8px 16px padding and a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Make only 'enter raid!' a lime (--acc) pill with --acc-ink text, or put a 3px lime bar on it. Remove the '!'. Place every label 16px above its station, not over the character.

findings.where: top-left and top-right HUD (the undercroft, 0 items in stash, $900, 0 xp, stash $0 bag $0)
findings.what: The text is 12 to 14px, below the 16px floor for anything read, and it sits on the black letterbox with no panel. The title is amber, not the lime accent. The money is the largest item, but it is crammed next to a bare '0' with a tiny 'xp'. The strings are spread across the screen with no grouping, and 'xp' should be 'sp' if it means score. The title is clipped against the left edge of the frame.
findings.fix: Put the title at 32px f-cond 700 in tx-1, with the subtitle at 16px tx-2 and 24px inset from the screen edge. Group the career numbers in one panel with a $ hero at 56px, and the other numbers at 16px tx-2. Use --acc, not amber, for the one highlighted item.

findings.what: Nine slots are shown, most of them dim, empty gun silhouettes, at about 100px each. It is a raid element sitting in the hub and it competes with the stations. The key numerals are 12px and unreadable from a couch. The focused slot has an amber border, not lime, so it clashes with the accent.
findings.fix: Hide the empty slots in the hub, or shrink the bar to 64px cells and show only the owned ones. Set the numerals at 16px, and use --acc for the 2px focus border.

findings.where: 'experimental feature may glitch' below the last pour
findings.what: It is a 16px white string with three asterisks on each side and no backing, placed over the floor art, and it reads as a debug note. It is an explaining sentence, which the owner has banned, and the asterisks look like a template.
findings.fix: Replace it with a 16px 'experimental' tag in --warn on a small panel pill attached to the label, with no asterisks and no sentence.

findings.where: player markers (pillager name, p1 tag, the rings under the characters)
findings.what: 'pillager' is amber 28px text and sits on top of an NPC. The 'p1' tag is a tiny box at the bottom, and the ring colours (amber and cyan) are shown with 12px numeral badges. The label is much bigger than the p1 tag, which is the actual identifier. The 'pillager' name competes with the station labels and it is not obvious which character is the player.
findings.fix: Set the name at 16px f-cond 600 with the p1 badge in the same pill (20px tall, 4px radius) directly above the head. Keep the ring colours as they are, since the colour choice is pending.

findings.where: control legend and toast ('l stick walk · ls jog · a use station' and 'pillager joined')
findings.what: The legend is 12px, below the 14px minimum, and sits right on top of the toast and the hotbar, with 'ls jog' and 'l stick' in odd casing. The toast has a white fill with dark text, which is the only light box on screen and does not match the dark panels. Both are stacked in about 50px just above the hotbar.
findings.fix: Set the legend at 14px minimum in tx-2, 16px above the hotbar, and the toast as a --ui-panel pill with tx-1 text 16px, 40px above the legend. Use the live pad glyphs (A, LS) instead of letters.

findings.what: It is a small green outlined chip in --ok green at about 14px on a lighter strip. Green means 'signed or built' in the guide, not 'device'. The chip is on a grey top bar that is part of the room art, so it looks pasted on.
findings.fix: Restyle it as a --ui-panel chip with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and tx-2 16px text, aligned with the other HUD panels at a 24px inset.

findings.where: station floor discs and room art
findings.what: The big translucent discs (purple, teal, amber, pink, brown) overlap each other, for instance the mainframe disc and the pink disc next to it, and they muddy the floor. The colours are close to the rarity and per-player tints and each has no meaning. The blue room is flat and busy with 12 NPCs, so the hierarchy is weak.
findings.fix: Draw one 2px ring per station at 40% opacity, in a single neutral (--ui-line-hi), and light it lime only when the player is in range. Remove the overlapping discs and the extra purple and pink fills.
